entries.title: Amos 1:1
segments: The earthquake; a very severe earthquake, as appears from

entries.title: Amos 1:2
segments:
Will roar--utter his voice; that is, pronounce his awful judgments. 
 
  From Zion--Jerusalem; because this was his earthly dwelling-place. 
 
  The top of Carmel; celebrated for its beauty and fertility.

God is infinitely holy, and hates all iniquity; he is infinite in power, and able to punish the mightiest sinner; he is infinitely true, and will fulfil all hiw threatenings to the wicked.  None that break his laws can escape his wrath, be they nations or individuals.

entries.title: Amos 1:3
segments: For three--and for four; that is, for oft-repeated transgressions. See note on

. 
 
  Damascus; the capital city of Syria, north-east of Palestine. 
 
  Threshed Gilead; these cruelties were exercised by Hazael king of Syria, as foretold by the prophet Elisha,

. 
 
  With threshing instruments of iron; that is, by dragging over them threshing sledges, set with sharp iron teeth.  Compare 2Sa12.31|. 
 
vv 3-15. 
 
The divine declaration, "he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh," holds good alike of mighty conquerors, and of the meanest among their subjects.  God will deal with unmerciful nations as they have dealt with their fellow nations.

entries.title: Amos 1:5
segments:
The plain of Aven; a valley near Damascus. 
 
  The house of Eden; or "Beth-eden," a royal city of Syria, on the Lebanon range. 
 
  Kir; a river, now called Kur, emptying into the Caspian sea, with the adjecent region.  See 2Ki 16.9.

entries.title: Amos 1:6
segments:
vv 6-8. 
 
  Gaza; Gaza, and the three other places named in connection with it, were the chief cities of Philistia. 
 
  The whole captivity; probably referring to the invasion recorded

  To deliver them up to Edom; the Edomites were the bitterest enemies of the Jews.

entries.title: Amos 1:9
segments: Delivered up the whole captivity; they seem to have invaded Judah in alliance with Philistia.  The two nations are named together by Joel as selling the children of the Jews for slaves.
The brotherly covenant; between David and Hiram, which was renewed by Solomon.

entries.title: Amos 1:11
segments: Did pursue his brother--kept his wrath; see

entries.title: Amos 1:13
segments: Gilead; a region east of the Jordan, south of Bashan, assigned by Moses to the tribes of Gad and Reuben.
Ammon lay to the east of it.

entries.title: Amos 1:14
segments: Rabbah; the chief city of Ammon.  According to Josephus, the Ammonites, as also the Moabites, were conquered by Nebuchadnezzar five years after the destruction of Jerusalem.
